articles.authors: Chong Li, Yun Xu, Jianbo Luo
institutions: School of Information Science and Engineering
articles.summary: Multi-view point cloud registration is challenging for yarn cheeses because their nearly axisymmetric geometry often leads to ambiguous point correspondences, particularly in regions with limited overlap and irregular surface contours. To address this problem, we propose rotation-axis-constrained shared-cross-section registration (RA-SCR) for structured-light volume measurement. The main contribution is a coupled pose–profile optimization method that jointly refines the three-degree-of-freedom residual pose of each view and a shared, axially layered cross-sectional model. …

articles.title: Accurate recognition of fractional orbital angular momentum of light in complex scenarios using physics-informed deep learning
articles.authors: Wenxi Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Yang Peng, Yin Xiao, Wen Chen
articles.summary: Light carrying fractional orbital angular momentum (FOAM) has received increasing attention in many fields due to its rich orbital angular momentum information. However, the recognition of FOAM beams in complex scenarios is challenging. Here we report physics-informed untrained neural networks (UNN) and polar mapping for accurate recognition of FOAM beams in complex scenarios. The physics-informed UNN is designed to retrieve high-quality FOAM patterns from a series of single-pixel light intensities collected through time-varying scattering media, and the retrieved FOAM patterns are further mapped in a polar coordinate. …

articles.title: Sculpting ultrafast mid-infrared light for solid-state high-harmonic generation
articles.authors: Bálint Kiss, Carmelo Rosales-Guzman, Stephan Fritzsche, Qiwen Zhan
institutions: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology
articles.summary: The ability to sculpt light in space, time, and polarization has revolutionized studies of light–matter interaction and enabled breakthroughs in optical communication, imaging, and ultrafast science. Among the many degrees of freedom of light, orbital angular momentum (OAM) further expands these capabilities by unlocking new regimes of control in information encoding, particle trapping and manipulation, and symmetry-driven selection rules. However, exploiting OAM to drive nonlinear, nonperturbative effects in solids remains challenging, especially in the mid-infrared (MIR) spectral region, key for accessing these effects in ambient air, where spatial light modulators are unavailable. …

articles.title: Twisted light-induced spatial and angular photonic spin splitting via quantum weak measurement
articles.authors: Dinesh Chandra Dey, Soumen Mandal, Anuradha Sett, Manik Pradhan
institutions: S N Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences
articles.journal: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
articles.summary: The photonic spin Hall effect (PSHE) at absorbing interfaces is governed by the interplay of spatial (S) and angular (A) spin-dependent contributions. Earlier studies based on non-vortex pointer states in lossless media predict vanishing photonic spin splitting (PSS) at the Brewster angle; however, these approaches face limitations under strong coupling regimes and near-orthogonal weak measurement conditions. Here, we demonstrate the coexistence of spatial and angular PSS at a monolayer WS2-SiO2/Si interface by employing vortex beams combined with weak value amplification (WVA). …

articles.title: Excitation of microbottle whispering-gallery modes using optical orbital angular momentum
articles.authors: Suresh Chejarla, Debojyoti Ray Chawdhury, Aneesh Vincent Veluthandath, Ganapathy Senthil Murugan, Prem B. Bisht, Balaji Srinivasan
articles.summary: We report a novel method for exciting whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in a microbottle resonator (MBR) using optical beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). The study presents both numerical and experimental analyses to demonstrate the coupling between the OAM beams and WGMs through the stem region of the MBR. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations are performed to investigate the propagation and overlap of OAM and WGM fields within the MBR geometry, revealing strong phase and spatial mode correlations near the caustic region. …

articles.title: MOPSO-enabled ultra-narrowband mechanically reconfigurable metasurface filter for terahertz applications
articles.authors: Jin-Yang Li, Yan-Qing Chen, Xue-Wei Ju, Yong-Zhen Liu, Hao-Bin Su, Bei-Yuan Liang, Han Ye, Jun-Long Liu, Shuo Liu, Xiang-Feng Wang
articles.journal: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
articles.summary: Terahertz (THz) communication and sensing systems require high-performance narrowband filters. However, designing these filters often involves strict efficiency bottlenecks and parameter trade-offs. To address this challenge, we propose an inverse design framework based on multi-objective particle swarm op-timization and use it to develop a bilayer ultra-narrowband me-chanically reconfigurable metasurface filter. Numerical parame-ter scanning reveals the potential for spacing-controlled fre-quency tuning, while measurements at three representative in-terlayer spacings experimentally verify the mechanical recon-figuration of the spectral response. …

We examine the emerging intersection of these two fields. We introduce the principal degrees of freedom of structured optical fields and summarize the distinctive hyperbolic dispersion, high wavevector modes, strong anisotropy, and enhanced light–matter interactions supported by multilayer, nanowire, and natural hyperbolic platforms. …

articles.authors: Jialing Jian, Qingyan Deng, Jianghong Wu, Jiaxi Yang, Yuting Ye, Bo Tang, Xiang Xu, Keyu Qian, Jiaxin Zhang, Junying Li, Hui Ma, Chuyu Zhong, Zhengjin Weng, Yuanfang Yu, Shaoqing Xiao, Hongtao Lin, Haiyan Nan, Lan Li
institutions: School of Integrated Circuits Jiangnan University Wuxi China
Institute of Microelectronics Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
articles.summary: Thermo‐optic (TO) modulators based on conventional materials face an unavoidable trade‐off among optical loss, power consumption, and response time. Here, we overcome this trilemma using a β′‐In 2 Se 3 microheater whose high electrical conductivity, optical transparency and low refractive index simultaneously enable ultralow propagation loss and high TO efficiency in the telecommunication band. This van der Waals material offers a potential pathway toward CMOS back‐end‐of‐line‐compatible integration with microring resonators (MRRs) using an ultrathin optical isolation layer, thereby facilitating fast thermal conduction and efficient thermal modulation. …

articles.title: A graphene-based tunable metasurface for on-demand terahertz beam-number switching with joint amplitude-phase optimization
articles.authors: Xingyu Guo, Yan Teng, Chun Li, Zhengwei Huang, Haobo Chen, Jiangtao Luo, Ziteng Wang, Ling Jiang
institutions: College of Information Science and Technology
articles.summary: On-demand beam-number switching is important for reconfigurable terahertz (THz) wavefront manipulation because it directly controls scattering-channel allocation, spatial coverage, and power distribution. However, it requires selective suppression of designated beams, stable preservation of remaining main beams, and adaptation to discrete device states. Here, we propose an on-demand THz beam-number switching method based on a graphene-tunable metasurface. A joint amplitude-phase particle swarm optimization model is developed by combining prior-phase inheritance, constrained joint amplitude-phase optimization, and device-aware quantized amplitude optimization. …

articles.title: Label-free counting of nanoparticles in a perfused microphysiological system by digital holography
articles.authors: Tomoyoshi Inoue, Iroha Okuda, Yasuhiro Ishihara
articles.summary: A wide variety of nanoparticles exist in the atmosphere, and there are concerns regarding the impact of their inhalation on the respiratory system. Recently, the respiratory effects of fine particles have been investigated using microfluidic systems (e.g., microphysiological systems), such as “lung-on-a-chip” devices; however, these studies often lack direct observation of the nanoparticles themselves. This is due to the absence of technology capable of detecting unlabeled particles under flow conditions. We have developed a holographic system that detects and counts nanoparticles flowing through a microphysiological system without labeling. …

articles.title: Arbitrary Reconfigurable Light‐Responsive Surface Topographies in Liquid Crystal Elastomer Films Using a Digital Micromirror Device
articles.authors: Ruth M. C. Verbroekken, Kelly Bour, Burcu Gumuscu, Albert P. H. J. Schenning
articles.summary: Arbitrary reconfigurable light‐responsive topographies enable repeated programming of surfaces with light, enabling applications in optics, biotechnology, microfluidics, and soft robotics. However, achieving such adaptive surfaces remains challenging. Here, we introduce digital micromirror device (DMD)‐based photo imprinting as a rapid, maskless technique for generating dynamic surface topographies in light‐responsive liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) films. The resulting surfaces exhibit reversible height modulations up to sub micrometers with lateral feature sizes down to 12.5 µm, and can be written, erased, and re‐written in arbitrary geometries. …

articles.title: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing
articles.authors: Zhaotong Cui, Binke Xia, Yuxiang Yang, Hongjing Li, Jingzheng Huang, Guihua Zeng
articles.summary: As sensor networks become more interconnected, sensitive information sharing among multiple users poses potential risks of information leakage, making privacy protection a critical challenge. To address this challenge, we quantify network privacy using the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR) and propose a protocol that enhances privacy through causal-order switching and probe squeezing. Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. …

articles.title: Polarization switching of double azimuthal backflow in two transverse orbital angular momentum superpositions
articles.authors: Zhen-Lai Wang
articles.summary: Optical backflow in the azimuthal direction can be generated by the interference of two rotating-wave structured light beams with distinct transverse topological charges and equal intensity. Here we show that the interference reverses both azimuthal components of the Poynting and the canonical momenta. Although these two momenta are not generally tied, they reverse jointly here: both acquire azimuthal backflow in a common angular sector, while their radial intervals can differ. The double backflow is switched solely by the polarizations of the two beams, without amplitude tuning. …

articles.title: Residual Errors Alter AI Chest-Radiograph Findings: Outage-Based Design of Free-Space Optical Links for Medical Image Delivery
articles.authors: Entidhar Mhawes Zghair, Seham Ahmed Hashem, Ali Mahdi Hammadi
articles.summary: Pathological chest radiographs are often assumed to be more vulnerable to channel impairments than normal ones. We simulated sending 250 NIH ChestX-ray14 radiographs from five diagnostic classes, in three payload formats sharing identical channel realizations, over a 1 km, 1550 nm free-space optical link with Gamma–Gamma fading, pointing errors and RS(255,204) coding. After an error event, diagnostic class explained 0.4–5% of the between-image variance in quality beyond grey-level statistics and JPEG size. A second, partially overlapping sample confirmed this, and a bit-level analysis explains why. …

articles.title: Binary Representation of Grayscale Images for DMD-Based Coherent Spatial Filtering Systems
articles.authors: Pavel A. Cheremkhin, Iuliia S. Lenkova, Daria V. Pavlenko, Vladislav G. Rodin, Anna V. Shifrina, Rostislav S. Starikov, Fedor A. Ushakov, Evgenii Yu. Zlokazov
institutions: Institute for Laser and Plasma Technologies
articles.summary: Fast optical data processing provides incredible opportunities for present-day and near-future tasks: pattern recognition, object tracking, beam shaping, development of diffractive neural networks, 3D-display and lithographic systems, etc. Digital micromirror devices (DMD) can display binary megapixel images with frame rates of tens of thousands Hz. However, grayscale images are more convenient for practical implementations. In this paper we analyzed several digital halftoning and binarization methods in search of the best one for a coherent DMD-based spatial filtering system. …

articles.title: Polarization-cloaked spatiotemporal topological knots
articles.authors: Yaning Zhou, Nianjia Zhang, Zhao Zhang, Chunhao Liang, Qian Cao, Houan Teng, Qiwen Zhan, Sergey A. Ponomarenko, Xu Guo, Yangjian Cai, Xin Liu
articles.summary: Spatiotemporally localized topological knots encode global connectivity within a moving space-time optical wavepacket, circumventing the requirement for spatial-only eigenmodes that extend throughout three-dimensional space-filling. In conventional modalities, this connectivity is identified directly from a scalar complex field. However, knotting optical knots with the polarization state of light proves difficult to realize for ultrafast localized wavepackets. …

articles.title: Turbulence Strength Estimation from Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams Using Multimode Fibre Speckle
articles.authors: Warwick G. C. Brown, Mitchell A. Cox
articles.summary: The strength of atmospheric turbulence governs how much the modes of a free-space optical link mix together. It is usually measured with a separate instrument or with a Gaussian probe beam, neither of which uses the beams that a structured-light link already carries. Here we show that the turbulence strength, expressed as the Fried parameter, can be estimated directly from multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams without knowing which modes are present. …

articles.title: Design of a compact, fast-switching high-voltage pulser for high-repetition-rate miniature time-of-flight mass spectrometers
articles.authors: Cao G, Huang Y, Zhu L, Zhou Z, Qi F
articles.summary: To meet the demand for miniaturized, low-power high-voltage pulse power supplies for time-of-flight mass spectrometers (TOF-MS), we designed a compact half-bridge push-pull pulse power supply. The power supply achieves a frequency range of 1-100 kHz, a maximum output voltage of 800 V, pulse-width adjustment in 0.1 μs steps, and a power consumption of ∼10 W. Electrical characterization shows that the rise time is less than 10 ns, overshoot is below 5%, amplitude and period stability are excellent, and the synchronization between positive and negative pulses is reliable. …
